diagnostic_evidence.quote: \item $A$ has an orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions $\{e_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$, spanning $\mathcal{L}^2(\mathcal{D})$, with corresponding eigenvalues $\{\mu_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$
Thus $A$ and $Q$ have eigenvalues $\mu_k = r^{-1}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{\alpha}$ and $\lambda_k = \sigma r^{-\gamma}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{-\beta}$

issues.failure_explanation: A non-decreasing sequence of positive eigenvalues satisfies $\lambda_k \geq \lambda_1 > 0$ for all $k$, while the bound $\lambda_k \leq C_2 k^{r_\lambda}$ with $r_\lambda < 0$ forces $\lambda_k \to 0$; the two requirements are jointly unsatisfiable for any nontrivial $Q$, so hypothesis (v) is vacuous as written. The intent is clear from (iv) and from the Laplacian example (where $\lambda_k = \sigma r^{-\gamma}(\kappa^2+\xi_k)^{-\beta}$ is non-increasing), and every proof uses only the bounds and the joint eigenbasis, never the monotonicity of $\lambda_k$.

failure_location.quote:
There exists an $r_{\lambda} < 0$ and a $C_2 > 0$ such that $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^\infty$ satisfies 

$$\lambda_k \leq C_2 k^{r_{\lambda}} .$$
where the eigenvalues $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ are indexed so that they are non-decreasing in $k$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change "non-decreasing" to "non-increasing" for $\{\lambda_k\}$ in (v) (or delete the monotonicity clause); no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Every result assuming Assumption operator (thm:spectral-convergence, cor:laplacian-spectral-convergence, thm:main-result) formally rests on an unsatisfiable hypothesis, but only the letter of the condition is affected; no rate, constant, or scope changes under the obvious repair.
issues.title: Assumption (v) demands a non-decreasing positive eigenvalue sequence bounded by a sequence tending to zero, which is unsatisfiable
issues.why_classification: A one-word repair restores consistency with (iv) and with the paper's own motivating example; all downstream results use only the eigenvalue bounds and the joint basis, so the method, conclusions, and advertised scope are completely preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that \Cref{assumption:operator}(i) and \Cref{assumption:operator}(ii) holds and that $\{X(t)\}_t$ satisfies \Cref{eq:stochastic-convolution}.

issues.failure_explanation: $\mathbb{E}[\omega_k(t)^2] = t\,\|Q^{1/2}e_k\|^2/\lambda_k$ equals $t$ only if $\|Q^{1/2}e_k\|^2 = \lambda_k$, i.e. only if $e_k$ is itself a $Q$-eigenfunction, which is assumption (iii) — not among the stated hypotheses (i),(ii). Under (i),(ii) alone, $\omega_k = \lambda_k^{-1/2}\langle W_Q, e_k\rangle$ may not even be well-defined ($e_k \notin D(Q^{1/2})$ in general) and is generally not a standard Wiener process; the proof's "by definition" assertion is incorrect, and the proof's own covariance computation uses $Q^{1/2}e_k = \sqrt{\lambda_k}e_k$.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore the processes $\{\omega_k(t)\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ are $\mathbb{R}$-valued, standard Wiener-processes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add assumption (iii) to the hypotheses of lemma:coefficient-representation, covering the standard-Wiener claim and the $\sqrt{\lambda_k}$ normalisation in eq:coefficient-integral.
issues.overall_effect: The representation eq:coefficient-integral and the standard-Wiener property are valid only under (iii), which every main theorem already assumes; the lemma's stated hypothesis list is too weak, but no downstream result changes once (iii) is included.
issues.title: Coefficient lemma claims standard Wiener processes under hypotheses that do not imply it
issues.why_classification: The repair is the addition of one already-standard hypothesis that all main results assume anyway; the lemma and everything built on it are unchanged in content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus $A$ and $Q$ have eigenvalues $\mu_k = r^{-1}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{\alpha}$ and $\lambda_k = \sigma r^{-\gamma}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{-\beta}$

issues.failure_explanation: From $\xi_k \geq C_\Delta k^{2/d}$ one obtains $\mu_k \geq r^{-1}C_\Delta^\alpha k^{2\alpha/d}$ and $\lambda_k \leq \sigma r^{-\gamma}C_\Delta^{-\beta}k^{-2\beta/d}$. The claimed bounds with the bare constant $C_\Delta$ require $C_\Delta^\alpha \geq C_\Delta$ and $C_\Delta \geq 1$ respectively, which need not hold (e.g. $C_\Delta < 1$ with $\alpha > 1$). Hence the choices $C_1 = r^{-1}C_\Delta$, $C_2 = \sigma r^{-\gamma}C_\Delta$ and the stated constant $C = \frac{\sigma r^{\gamma-1}C_\Delta^{2-2\gamma}\Gamma(2\gamma-1)}{\Gamma(\gamma)^2}\frac{d}{2\nu}$ are unjustified; the constant following from the valid bounds is $\frac{\sigma r^{\gamma-1}C_\Delta^{-\beta-\alpha(2\gamma-1)}\Gamma(2\gamma-1)}{\Gamma(\gamma)^2}\frac{d}{2\nu}$.

failure_location.quote: and $\{\mu_k\}_{k = 1}^\infty$ and $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ satisfy the bounds $r^{-1} C_\Delta k^{\frac{2 \alpha}{d}}\leq \mu_k$ and $\lambda_k \leq \sigma r^{-\gamma} C_\Delta k^{- \frac{2 \beta}{d}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bounds by $\mu_k \geq r^{-1}C_\Delta^\alpha k^{2\alpha/d}$ and $\lambda_k \leq \sigma r^{-\gamma}C_\Delta^{-\beta}k^{-2\beta/d}$ and update the constant accordingly; the rate and hypotheses are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence rate $M^{-2\nu/d}$ of cor:laplacian-spectral-convergence is unaffected, but its explicit error constant is wrong in general; the spectral convergence experiments, which rely only on the rate $\nu_s/2$, are unaffected.
issues.title: Laplacian spectral corollary derives eigenvalue bounds and error constant with wrong powers of $C_\Delta$
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local re-derivation of constants with no new argument; the rate, which is the substance of the corollary, is preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consequently, under stated assumptions, for all $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$

If $\ell < n$, then by \Cref{lem:boundedness-p0-inequalities} we have that 

$$(*) \lesssim 2 \alpha g_\ell ((t_n - t_{\ell - 1})^{\gamma} - (t_n - t_\ell)^{\gamma}) = 2 \alpha g_\ell \gamma \int_{t_{\ell - 1}}^{t_\ell} f_{t_n}(s) \, \text{d}s\, .$$

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is stated and proved for $\alpha > 0$, but the "Consequently" chains are claimed for all $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ without proof; for $\alpha < 0$ the displayed inequalities reverse. lem:boundedness-p0 invokes the lemma with the exponents $\gamma-1$ and $2\gamma-2$, which are negative for $\gamma < 1$ — a regime cor:order-0-method explicitly covers. The claimed bounds do remain true (the ratios are controlled by constants of the form $(1+\theta\overline{k})^{|\alpha|}$ and $\overline{k}^{1-\gamma}$), so the repair is a short addition.

failure_location.quote: It is trivial that $(t_n - \Tilde{s}_\ell)^\alpha \leq (t_n - t_{\ell - 1})^{\alpha}$ and $(t_n - t_\ell)^\alpha \leq (t_n - \Tilde{s}_\ell)^{\alpha}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend the proof of lem:boundedness-p0-inequalities to negative exponents (bound the ratios $\frac{t_n-t_{\ell-1}}{t_n-\Tilde{s}_\ell}$ and $\frac{t_n-\Tilde{s}_\ell}{t_n-t_\ell}$ by $1+\theta\overline{k}$ and $1+(1-\theta)\\overline{k}$), or bound the cross and squared terms in lem:boundedness-p0 directly; no statement changes.
issues.overall_effect: lem:boundedness-p0 and cor:order-0-method remain true, but their proofs are incomplete for $\gamma \in (1/2,1)$; the temporal convergence theory for piecewise-constant sampling rests on this repairable gap.
issues.title: Mesh-ratio inequalities are proved only for positive exponents but are used with negative exponents for $\gamma < 1$
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local estimate; every claim, constant-dependence, and rate in the lemma and its corollary is preserved.
